Report Details

Permit API: 115-22174
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-12
Comments: Arrived on location at 08:20. Onsite to initiate a 72 hr. PBUT on all (4) Howell M wells, the 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H wells. I met with Cabot O&G Reps., Devin Lyke, Marshall McCarty, Keenan Small and James Brown. Deven and Marshall were checking and calibrating the transducers on the (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli of all four wells before starting the PBUT. The (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli vents were connected together and going to a common poly vent tank (see photo #3), that was shared with the vent lines of the 2H, 4H and 8H wells. There was gas detected at the tank. No gas or flow checks were taken at the block and bleed prier to the the start of the PBUT because of the possibility of commingling. The 2H is temporarily plugged because of stimulation operations at the Powers M pad but the 2H, 4H and 8H wells will remain in production during the PBUT. PBUT was initiated on all wells (20x13), (13x9) and (9x5) annuli at ~ 09:28 on 6/12/20. Left location at 09:35.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/04/2025 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Donegal Township, Washington county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/04/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8223350
Permit API: 125-29142
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Donegal Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/04/2025
Comments: On 03/04/2025, a follow up inspection was conducted at the DMC Well site, for violations cited on 2/21/2025 (Inspection ID: 3922642, Enforcement ID: 438876).Violations included 78a57a, 78a54, 91.34(a) and SWMA 301.PA DEP conductivity probe calibrated on 03/04/2025.During the inspection the following was observed:-The Act 9 sign was present at site entrance (Photo 1).-The previously impacted area, noted in Inspection Report (IR) 3922642, located on the northwest side of the well pad was observed. A layer of a white, crusty substance was observed on the soil located in front of the large, gray electrical box noted in IR 3922642 (Photos 2-6).-Field conductivity screening was conducted near the large, gray electrical box. Field conductivity readings between 0.993 ms/cm (993 s/cm) and 14.17 ms/cm were observed. This area had not been previously remediated due to the proximity to the electrical equipment, as discussed with the operator (Photos 7-11).-Pooled fluid was observed located directly adjacent to secondary containment. An elevated field conductivity reading of 18.60 ms/cm was observed within the fluid. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a). Outstanding violations are being issued for the pooled fluid demonstrating elevated conductivity (Photos 12-14).-Damp material was observed along the edge of the secondary containment. An elevated field conductivity reading of 8.74 ms/cm was observed (Photos 15-16).-Pooled fluid was observed on a driving lane near the site entrance on the northeast side of the well pad. Field conductivity readings between 0.470 ms/cm (470 s/cm) and 5.85 ms/cm were observed (Photos 17-21).Determination:Outstanding violations issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/19/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/19/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 992310
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 944851
Permit API: 081-21874
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/10/2022
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess site conditions after a reported release of produced water to Pad A on 11/17/21. On Pad A, additional excavation has taken place since the produced water tanks and their containment have been moved to another location on the pad. A trench has been dug along the edge of the pad where a stormwater channel was located at the pad edge behind the GPUs and the previous location of the produced water tanks. Creston Environmental representatives were on location and informed me that the soil and water electrical conductivities (EC) were all below 2 mS/cm on site. I screened a few puddles on the pad surface near the excavated trench and these had EC readings between 1.7 and 1.9 mS/cm. A battery of frac tanks is also present on Pad A within secondary containment. The tanks and containments appear to be in good condition. On Pad B, some trucks are staging on the pad. The nine wells have been drilled but they have not yet been fraced. The pad is snow-covered. Violations remain outstanding for the release on Pad A from 11/17/21.

Comments: Follow up inspection of the Export Fuel 1 well conducted on 8/9/2022. Arrived on location at 10:04. A follow up inspection was conducted on 4/15/2022 (Inspection Record No. 3347700). This inspection found that none of the previously cited violations had been addressed or responded to and all violations remained outstanding. Comments: On 3/27/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4000998, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4 and 6). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 8). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 5 and 7). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 10 and 11). Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photo 2).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4000998 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: On June 3, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Malinky well pad in Smith Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination request was approved for this site on August 21, 2019. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3972958, where remediation efforts had been reportedly completed in response to the 5/01/2025 200-gallon diethylene glycol release. However, violations were left outstanding as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) is onsite and appears to contain the information required by 78a.55 (see photo 3). No visual evidence of any remaining impacted material was observed in the formerly impacted area (see photos 4 and 5). The GPU units connected to the wells onsite which were drilled after the promulgation of 78a are placed within secondary containment (see photo 6). The GPU units connected to the wells onsite which predate promulgation of 78a are not placed within secondary containment (see photo 7). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 8). Well 2H is equipped with a well tag with no staining or evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it, and it appears to be in production (see photos 10 and 11). There are six additional wells onsite that also appear to be in production.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that visual remediation of the impacted area has been successfully completed. However, violations issued from IR 3969681 shall remain outstanding, as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.

Comments: At time of inspection: On site for a post-plugging inspection of the Heuer 1V (117-20767) well to check for gas at a plugged well. Met with Repsol rep. Shaun Smith. Eric Hottenstein (Chesapeake) estimated that 1.5 barrels sprayed on containment and 1 barrel sprayed off containment.At the time of arrival (1000 hours), we met with Eric Hottenstein at the pad entrance. At approximately 1015 hours, Jon Zwetzig (Chesapeake Field Safety Representative) met with us and stated we were allowed back onsite along the perimeter of the pad. Mr. Zwetzig and Mr. Hottenstein led us toward the southern edge of the pad where the oil based mud sprayed off containment. From the point of the spraying event to the edge of containment was approximately 100' (photo # 2, 3). An additional 60' of vegetation had been excavated from the southern edge of the pad out toward the tree line (photo # 5). The gas kick took place while drilling the 5H well according to Mr. Zwetzig.According to Mr. Hottenstein, the majority of the sprayed oil based mud was captured by the dense vegetation off of the southern edge of the pad, with visually minimal oil based mud making contact with the ground (photo # 13). A dark staining was visually observed on the vegetation along the existing tree line that remained to be excavated (photo # 7, 8, 10, 13) and the smell of oil was heavy along the impacted treeline. Mr. Hottenstein stated that Chesapeake plans to continue excavating the impacted vegetation and then soil samples are to be taken from the roughly 60' x 60' excavated location (photo # 12). Sampling is to be conducted by Creston Environmental. Excavated vegetation and materials are being staged within containers at the Mad Dog lcoation, where additional plastic liner is being laid down for containment.Mr. Hottenstein stated that once excavation and soil sampling is completed, the excavated grounds will be hydroseeded and additional silt sock will be laid down gradient in order to mitigate any potential erosion and sedimentation.Mr. Hottenstein stated that Chesapeake will be pursuing Act 2 remediation.The release of a regulated substance to the ground surface is in violation of CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a). Due to an undetermined amount of regulated substance being released to the ground surface, please refer to 78a.66 regarding remediating releases of regulated substances on well sites.We departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the report of a discharge of crude oil from this well on April 2, 2022. The release occurred as a result of vandalism, in which a third party individual who had climbed the pump jack damaged a valve on the gathering lime riser when jumping off of the jack. Pennsylvania State Police investigated the incident and the responsible party was found and reportedly admitted what had happened. Upon my arrival, repairs have been made and there was no active discharge. The majority of the released product remained on the well site and a portion of the spur road leading to it. The contaminated soil/rock from the location and road (approximately 3-5 tons) has been excavated and placed on a contained pit liner for upcoming disposal. There was no evidence that any of the released product entered the road ditch that runs alongside the spur road. No watercourses were impacted as a result of this incident. Crews were in the process of removing oil soaked leaves along the edge of the road/location. After that work is completed, no additional remediation measures appear necessary, as the ground underneath the leaves does not appear to be impacted per field screening. A future inspection will be conducted to evaluate if any additional measures are necessary.

Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Permit API: 083-57144
Unconventional: No
County: McKean

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/09/2022
Comments: This conventional well has recently been produced with a pump jack, there was no activity on this location or throughout the Cole Creek lease during this inspection.A tank battery consisting of a 210 bbl steel stock tank and a poly brine/production water tank is located approximately 150 feet to the south of this well. These tanks are contained by an earthen dyking which has been lined and partially filled with gravel. Holes have formed throughout the exposed portion of the liner along the upper edge of the containment wall.Fluid was trickling out of the containment drain pipe into the roadside ditch upon my arrival at the tank battery. There was no supervision of this discharge and the drain is not equipped with a valve. A shower drain cover was fitted onto the inlet of this drain. The specific conductivity (SPC) of the fluid inside of the containment exceeded the upper threshold of my field meter (20,000 uS/cm). Pooled fluid in the ditch was also greater than 20,000 uS/cm. Deer tracks are abundant around the pooled fluid in the roadside ditch. This evidence suggests that the fluid being discharged from the containment drain is production water/brine. An SAC 941 sample was collected from the fluid discharging from the drain. The fluid in the roadside ditch flowed through a cross culvert and into a forested area. Poor road conditions have allowed stormwater to run off of the road surface above this culvert, which allowed the released fluid to migrate further into the forested area. Elevated SPC of pooled water and soil (along with stressed vegetation) was observed in various pathways across the forest floor west of the tank battery for approximately 200 feet downslope of the tank battery. The most downward extent of the apparent impacted soil (near a property boundary/corner marker) is approaching a channel (currently dry) that develops into an unnamed tributary of Cole Creek.After this inspection, I spoke with Justin Hansen of Bull Run to discuss the aforementioned issues along with concerns regarding the roads, site identification and actions necessary to consider this well site restored. In order to consider utilizing the containment drain, the fluid that is currently pooled inside of the containment will need to be removed along with the saturated gravel. Prior to any future discharges from the drain, the water should be tested as per the regulations to ensure it meets the criteria to be released under sufficient supervision.Future inspections will be conducted to review the current state of affairs with Bull Run personnel and evaluate remediation measures outside of the containment as they take place.

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8230099
Permit API: 129-24095
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Rostraver Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2025
Comments: On April 17, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Mountain View LTV 2 well located in Rostraver Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3715546 where violations were issued for a release and for IR 3882155 where violations were continued due to site conditions being unchanged. The LTV 2 site is located within abandoned coal mine land and therefore the well site is composed of coal refuge. Mountain View Operator Dave Lindahl informed the Department via email (documented in IR 3797419) that this abandoned coal mine land is to be remediated by the Department's Clean Streams Program and that this well site is included in their remediationplans. Mr. Lindahl also stated that what the Department observes to be a release from production equipment at the well site's entrance is actually runoff from the spoil piles upslope of the well site.During IR 3882155, the Department observed the spoil piles Mr. Lindahl mentioned, however, the Department did not observe any evidence of erosion channels or a distinct pathway that goes from the spoil piles and leads to the entrance of the well site where the release is observed to be. A distinct change in the ground level is observed in the release arearight next to the wellhead and separator piping, which further supports the notion that fluid from this production equipment is where the release originated. This in conjunction with elevated soil conductivity readings in this area lead the Department in IR 3715546 to again recommend the Operator remediate the release in accordance with the Department's policy for small spills despite the Clean Streams Program's remediation site plans including the LTV 2 site within it.At the time of this inspection, site conditions appeared to be unchanged. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it and a production tank was observed to be lopsided and sinking into the ground. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of the production equipment on site, however, the spill area documented in IR 3715546 still appears to be present. Fluid is observed to be pooled starting at the wellhead and proceeding to exit the well site and flow downslope. Based on unchanged site conditions, and the Operator's notion of this not being a release but rather spoil pile runoff, the Department collected soil samples for SAC 960 (General Chemistry) and UV (Ultra Violet)/IR (Infra Red) analysis at the following locations:Background 1 - Lat: 40.19595, Long: -79.76428 - In vegetation adjacent to well site 0.1249 mS soil conductivity readingBackground 2 - Lat: 40.19602, Long: -79.76539 - In coal mine refuse right below spoil piles 0.1388 mS soil conductivity readingLocation 1 - Lat: 40.19601, Long: -79.76466 - At base of wellhead where release appears to originate 0.539 mS soil conductivity readingLocation 2 - Lat: 40.19607, Long: -79.76459 - In spill pathway 0.782 mS soil conductivity readingAll samples were legal sealed and sent to the Department's Bureau of Laboratories in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania.Based on today's inspection, violations issue during IR 3715546 shall be continued due to site conditions remaining unchanged.

These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a temporary poly vent tank via rubber lines. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Craig Shores and Trey Sites, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andy Sallaway and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the HUNTER Pad wells. - HUNTER 5H: (20x13): 3.0 psi.; 68 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:17 ** (13x9): 277 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 ** (9x5): 327 psi.; 85 % CH4; Sample collected at 10:27 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:20. - HUNTER 6H: (20x13): 17.0 psi.; 65 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 ** (13x9): 169.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:37 ** (9x5): 549.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:40. - HUNTER 22HC: (20x13): 24.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:45 ** (13x9): 226.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:49 ** (9x5): 396.0 psi.; 92 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 10:50. - HUNTER 21HC: (20x13): 44.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sampled collected @ 10:55 ** (13x9): 268.0 psi.; 90 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 ** (9x5): 131.0 psi.; 87 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:07 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:00. - HUNTER 23HC: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 255.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:13 (9x5): 321.0 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:20 (20x13) annulus was opened back to venting to atmosphere via Sentry valve @ 11:30. - All (5) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to poly tank @ 11:45. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (20x13) and the(13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the HUNTER 23HC (20x13) annulus. This is indicative of defective cement. Since the presence of gas was detected in the HUNTER 5H well (20x13) annulus was not addressed in previous responses received, the Dept. requests in writing, by 7/4/20, how CALLC plans to address this defective condition.

Comments: This well was drilled in a forested area off of Point View Road in March 2006. Since the most recent inspection of the site on 8/30/2021 (Inspection Record # 3242810), work has been started on remediation of the site. A spill was reported to the Department on 11:03 AM on August 27, 2021. The spill occurred from a broken copper line attached to the wellhead. The estimated volume lost from this spill was 2 bbl. During this inspection, it was noted that the production equipment has been disconnected and staged along the edge of the restored site. Stressed vegetation and contaminated soil has been removed from the site. A response to the NOV has been received by the Department. The violations at the site can be closed when the contaminated soil has been replaced, the site has been graded to final contours, and the manifest and tipping information for soil disposal has been received by the Department.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/02/2024
Comments: On December 2, 2024, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a reported release that reportedly occurred on site on December 1, 2024 at 1:15pm. The incident was reported to the Department by Nate Smeill (Range Resources) on December 1, 2024 at 2:29pm as an approximate 10 gallon release of produced water to the gravel well pad. The Department spoke with Smiell via phone call upon arriving to the site at 11:50am. According to Smiell:- the 10 gallon release of produced water was determined to be a visual estimate in terms of amount released- the release occurred when the driver of a water truck hauler failed to close the bleeder valve on the truck when filling the truck with produced water- all impacted material was placed into the roll off box that remains on site at this time- only work left to be done for remediation is new gravel back fill at area of release- a spill report will be sent to the Department later todayThe ESCGP (ESX17-003-0002) was issued on 9/20/2017 and was set to expire on 9/19/2022. The Notice of Termination (NOT) was submitted by the Operator on 11/3/2020 and was approved by the Department on 11/16/2020.Act 9 sign present on site. Access road is in good condition with no erosion and/or sedimentation (ES) issues observed. Emergency Response Plan, Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, and ESCGP plans are all present on site. Area of where the produced water was released is observed in Photos 8-9, the roll off box containing the impacted material is observed in Photo 10, and a measure of specific conductivity within the area of release is observed in Photo 11, showing proper remediation of the area in accordance with 78a.66(c)(1).Violations for the release are being issued and immediately corrected.
